title: Which module pulls the expensive PDF renderer into shipit start-up
prompt:
`python3 -m shipit --help` has become slow. Profiling shows most of the time goes into importing `shipit.render.pdf`, even though the README says only commands that actually produce a PDF should load it. I want to fix this at the source, so I need to know which module's import-time (top-level) code is pulling it in during start-up.

Precisely: when `python3 -m shipit --help` runs from the root of this repository, at the moment `shipit.render.pdf` is first imported, which is the innermost module on the call stack that is still in the middle of executing its own top-level code (not counting `shipit.render.pdf` itself)?

Answer with its dotted module name (e.g. `shipit.something`).
verify:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import contextlib, io, runpy, sys
TARGET = 'shipit.render.pdf'
found = []

class Spy:
    """On the first import of TARGET, record the innermost module still running top-level code."""
    def find_spec(self, name, path=None, target=None):
        if name == TARGET and not found:
            frame = sys._getframe(1)
            while frame is not None:
                mod = frame.f_globals.get('__name__', '')
                if frame.f_code.co_name == '<module>' and mod.startswith('shipit') and mod != TARGET:
                    found.append(mod)
                    break
                frame = frame.f_back
        return None

sys.meta_path.insert(0, Spy())
sys.argv = ['shipit', '--help']
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
    try:
        runpy.run_module('shipit', run_name='__main__')
    except SystemExit:
        pass
assert TARGET in sys.modules, 'pdf was not imported'
print(found[0])
EOF
